questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to southern Europe, Italy, Spain or Portugal, and with my education it left me with Milan as the only option.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really loved living in Italy, meeting new people, both other danish students (which there were many of) but also other international and italian students. The only reason why it's 9/10 and not 10/10 would be some of the educational aspects such as logistics, teachers and exam methods.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I did my exchange with 3 friends from my study, so finding all information was easier, being 4 people searching for the correct information etc., but it was not the most easy as I remember. Especially doing the logistics with choosing courses was pretty difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office in Milan had wrote us an email, etc. and we could also ask the administration at the Erasmus office there, when we went to register our date of arrival. But we had to ask many questions to figure everything out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were some different Erasmus meeting days in the beginning, but you had to be acquainted with the Erasmus email or instagram in order to know this. The university itself had no such introduction day or campus tour or anything. It would have been nice to have a campus tour and knowledge of reading spots and libraries etc. around campus.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found housing through some friends of friends that had been in Milan on exchange prior to us, so we ended up booking their apartment through an italian accommodation website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: We lived 45 minutes from our campus (Citta Studi) but much closer to centrum. We liked it this way, and the metro system was fine for transportation (when they were not on a strike..)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it can be difficult to find accommodation, but we were looking for apartments in good time, and were pretty lucky I guess.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the course registration and planning of the different courses a bit difficult and confusing on the website.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't recall any help, other than writing to the university Erasmus office for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most classes I wanted without any overlapping courses, but it was a big puzzle.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Examine the different courses from the course list on the university website before arriving, but don't expect to get the courses you want, since the schedules are finished one week before the courses start, so you cannot plan the final classes from home. And I would personally recommend not taking too many classes with oral exams, since they are very much different from the exams in Denmark, and not very nice to attend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My course in Cell Theory and Gene Silencing was pretty interesting, and relevant also to my education at UCPH, however some of the other courses were not at a very high academic level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MA courses were the only once in english, and the level of the courses was generally lower than those at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was almost exclusively lectures, 2 hours long and often without breaks. We didn't have other teaching material than the powerpoints from our professors, but that was enough to study for the exams. However, I missed the different SAU and theoretical exercises from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cell Therapy and Gene Silencing (7 ETCS), Molecular Pharmacology and Immunology (6 ETCS),  Molecular Bioinformatics (6 ETCS) and Genetics, cellular and Molecular Biology (12 ETCS). 31 ETCS in total.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cell Therapy and Gene Silencing (7 ETCS) was pretty interesting I think, and nice teachers, some laboratory classes as well.
Molecular Pharmacology and Immunology (6 ETCS) would have been easier if we had had Immunology before, but it's manageable without.
Molecular Bioinformatics (6 ETCS) was not the most interesting I must admit, but the exam was relatively easy.
Genetics, Cellular and Molecular Biology (12 ETCS) was easier since the curriculum covered many courses that I have had before at UCPH, however the exam was oral, and the teachers (one of them in particular) was kind of rude. So I would't necessarily recommend this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The only thing I can think of is that we had to buy a lab coat that costs 38 euros (I forgot mine in DK)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation was very cheap, the ATM card for students were only 22 euros pr. month, also groceries in general are very delicious and cheap. Going to the gym however is very very expensive in Milan, which came as quite a shock.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The host institution had some different sports teams you could apply for, but I didn't attend any of those. The city in general has a lot to offer, so I enjoyed using those instead (not for sports however).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some different events, and also lots of different Erasmus events, so it was pretty easy to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend maybe attending some of the Erasmus meetings and/or events especially in the beginning, and then just talk to people if they seem nice, and ask them out for a coffee friend-date or dinner or something.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I especially recommend taking some weekend trips to the surrounding cities in Italy via train or bus. In the summer I went to Genova and Sori. In the fall I went hiking at Como lake, I also visited Bologna, which is so beautiful and also full of students, and Bergamo for Christmas markets. In january  went skiing in Aprica, which was very nice as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, it's not exactly a culture shock living in Italy, but there are maybe some different étiquettes when addressing elder and professors, compared to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just approach the students in your classes, they are very friendly and helpful in general! (They often go out for aperativo after classes in the afternoon)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many places, they don't speak good english, so that can be a bit challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the social life and the more relaxed italian mentality.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to approach someone you don't know. If you cannot figure something out at our host institution, write to the Erasmus coordinators and just know that the Italians are not very structured or well organized, so sometimes it can longer to figure everything out, but just remember that everything will be solved at the end, so don't stress too much about it (even though it can be a bit frustrating, coming from Denmark:)).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing other than their slower and less optimized organization and coordination skills.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural experience and meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was not knowing everything in advance, and sometimes figuring things out in the last minute, but it worked out always, so it taught me that I can let go of control a bit more than I initially would.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
